newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank Montreal's Barrett defends dual role.
newsitem.headline: Bank Montreal's Barrett defends dual role.

text.p: Bank of Montreal chairman Matthew Barrett defended his dual role as chairman and chief executive officer on Tuesday, in the face of proposals from two pension funds which could require two other banks to split the jobs.
Speaking to reporters after the bank's annual meeting, Barrett said the Bank of Montreal has sufficient safeguards in place to meet investor concerns over executive accountability.
"The central concern is what safeguards are there to make sure the two hats are being worn appropriately," Barrett said.

"In our own case, we've included several safeguards in the governance process of the bank which have eliminated entirely the concerns people would have about the chairman and CEO being one and the same," Barrett said.

He was commenting on a newspaper report on Tuesday that Canada's two largest pension funds may support a shareholder's proposal to divide the jobs of chairman and chief executive officer at Royal Bank of Canada and National Bank of Canada. The Caisse de depot et placement du Quebec and the Ontario Teachers Pension Plan Board both have significant holdings in Royal Bank and National Bank.

Royal Bank and National Bank were forced to include the resolution after a Quebec court supported shareholder Yves Michaud's bid to have it and other resolutions restricting executive pay put to a vote at the banks' annual meetings in March.
Barrett said he is willing to examine the issue in light of recent concerns, but he warned against making arbitrary decisions that are not based on sound management principles.
Barrett also called on the federal government to change Canada's banking rules, which he said are unclear on this subject.
